text: The four consumed rows of the settlement step are class C dependencies in fact: the proposal of rwb-agent (P10), the approval of rwb-decision (P7), the booking of rwb-treatment (S2) and the case-move answer of rwb-case (P3). The metadata contract-dependency row of both slices stays None as the plan gives it, and both stories build against the owners' published documents and fakes on Day 1.
why: The ownership rows of S4 list two tables, five REST operations, no event and no job, so none of the four effects can happen in this service; the plan's C row for both slices is an empty list, and no source names a published operation for any of the four, so a C row cannot be written with a real name.

why: TSD S4 T5.2 names the interfaces P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6 with no operation, T-A.1 lists five S4 operations only, the FSD A2.13.2 names the integration point as Workbench only, and no source gives the field list of a proposal, an approval, a booking or a case move.

text: The settlement proposal arrives as a signal of LitigationWorkflow on task queue rwb-litigation; no event and no Schedule is declared, and the officer enters the proposal on SCR-19 where the source of the proposal is the officer rather than the customer or the firm.
why: Legacy AC1 says the user acts on the screen and AC2 says the customer or the firm proposes the settlement, FSD S4 A2.13.2 is a user feature and A2.13.4.4 declares no system background event, and DP-09 is not in the pattern set of this key, so the arrival cannot be an event of this service.

text: The hold 'hold the litigation rather than withdraw it' is the stage state LITIGATION_HELD of LitigationWorkflow, answered to rwb-case as the case move; legal_action.status keeps FILED, the withdrawal stays with R-LIT-39, no held value is added to LOV-LEGAL-STATUS and no column is added to legal_action.
why: R-LIT-37 holds the litigation while R-LIT-39 withdraws the case only when the treatment completes, LOV-LEGAL-STATUS of TSD S4 T3.2 has no held value, and legal_action of T3.1 has no hold column, so the hold cannot be a column or a list value without inventing one.

text: The approver named by the limit is a delegated-authority approver of the DoA matrix governed in rwb-decision (P7), not a Litigation role; the stories consume the approver and the approval on the owner's contract, add no Litigation right for the approval, and read the D7.4 limit and the rule rows of R-LIT-36 to R-LIT-38 from the package in force.
why: The legacy Permission checks table gives the Litigation capability area C and R only, the FSD A2.13.3.3 names the Head of Litigation and the product head as also-users, and the context pack slide 3 notes place the approver within their delegated authority under the DoA Matrix v2, which is a decision-service fact and not a litigation right.

text: SCR-18 Notice approval is carried read-only as the notice context of the case and shows no settlement state; the step is worked on SCR-19 Litigation workspace, whose legacy states pack, instructed, filed, hearing and judgment are kept and joined by offered at court, held, rejected, not recorded and refused.
